value: Whole-brain analysis of the Cigarette Cues versus Neutral Cues contrast across all participants revealed significant activation in brain regions implicated in cue reactivity, including the left nucleus accumbens, and bilateral precuneus, thalamus, and caudate nucleus.

A priori defined ROI analyses revealed significant medication effects, controlling for FTND score, in the precuneus, left NAcc, bilateral rostral ACC, and right SFG; no medication effects were observed for the ventral anterior insula.

All medications suppressed left nucleus accumbens activation relative to placebo, suggesting the possibility that both medications, alone and in combination, reduce neural signals associated with appetitive behavior.
